packageRules.description: HOLD bytemare/ecc + bytemare/secret-sharing (and their matching transitive bytemare/hash, bytemare/hash2curve, bytemare/secp256k1) at their current pins. github.com/bytemare/frost is pinned to an untagged 2024 commit — no upstream tags/releases exist, so Renovate cannot track or bump frost itself — and that pinned frost commit does not build against ecc v0.10.0 (internal/hashing.go, internal/lambda.go: signature/return-value mismatches). Confirmed in a322214 (2026-09-03) and reconfirmed independently the same day when Renovate re-proposed the identical bump in MR!119 and hit the same build/lint/test:unit failures. The only newer frost commit that compiles against ecc v0.10.0 (316cadd, 2026-06-16) is a large breaking rewrite of frost's public API and also requires secret-sharing >= v0.8.1-pre, whose keys.KeyShare/PublicKeyShare API went from exported fields to unexported/method-based — that would mean rewriting internal/frost/{coordinator,dkg,remote_signer}.go (our threshold-signing/DKG wrapper) as its own reviewed piece of work, not inside a dependency-bump MR. Adopting it also forces go.mod's `go` directive above the standing floor (see ci-templates' gomod/go enabled:false rule), which is a separate hard no. REMOVE THIS RULE once frost is tagged with a release that supports ecc v0.10.0 without the secret-sharing breaking rewrite, or once the coordinator/dkg/remote_signer migration has been done and reviewed on its own branch.

NEVER @cloistr/ui 0.44.0 or 0.44.1: an import cycle in components/ServiceMenu throws 'Cannot access defaultServices before initialization' at module load and blanks the whole UI (reproduced 2026-10-07: 0.43.0 and 0.44.2 render, 0.44.0/0.44.1 throw). ui/package.json is pinned to 0.44.2; this rule only stops a regression back onto the broken versions. Safe to remove once the pin is past 0.44.x.

frost-wasm crypto crates move TOGETHER or not at all. k256/elliptic-curve/sha2/hkdf share the RustCrypto digest/traits generation, and getrandom/rand_core/rand_chacha share the rand_core generation; bumping any one alone does not compile (e.g. sha2 0.11 vs hkdf 0.12, rand_core 0.10 has no OsRng). Grouped into one MR so the test:frost-wasm job judges the whole set. Moving to rand_core 0.10 / getrandom 0.4 / k256 0.14 is a source change (OsRng is gone), not a version bump.
